description: The shared corpus for the one timestamp decision procedure: given a metadata object and an ordered list of keys, produce an instant or a stated reason no instant could be produced. Every expression of the rule (frontend/src/lib/epoch.ts, seance_core::timestamp, and the histogram SQL) is pinned by THIS file, so a divergence between them is a failing test rather than a silent disagreement about when something happened. Each expectation below was measured against the shipping browser reader before it was written down; where the browser's answer is wrong, the row says so in its name rather than hiding it.

schema.name: what the row pins, in a sentence
schema.keys: the ordered key list the procedure is given; the FIRST key that yields an instant wins
schema.input: the metadata object, as a parser would have written it
schema.expect: exactly one of { placed_secs, confidence: as_written | by_rescue } | { unplaceable: "value" } | { unplaceable: "absent" }

confidence.as_written: read in the unit the record's contract states (whole Unix seconds), or parsed from a written date-time that carries its own UTC offset
confidence.by_rescue: placed only by assuming which unit the parser used - milliseconds, microseconds or Windows FILETIME ticks. A weaker fact than as_written, and it must be reported as one.

rows.name: whole Unix seconds, the documented contract for `date`
a genuine pre-1973 instant is BELOW the seconds band and cannot be placed at all
1e8 exactly is outside the band (the comparison is strictly greater)
one second past the band floor is placed: 1973-03-03
0 is a present value with no admissible reading, never 1970-01-01
a negative whole-seconds value is not placed
millisecond magnitude is placed only by assuming the unit
millisecond magnitude as an integer-literal string, same rescue
microsecond magnitude falls into the FILETIME band and lands in 1606 - the wrong answer the reader gives today, and why wave 1C fixes the unit at the source
Windows FILETIME ticks are placed by rescue: 2024-01-17
a FILETIME string is converted exactly, one tick below a second boundary
an integer literal too large for any epoch is not placed
CallLog writes `timestamp` and no `date`; the second key is read
KEY PRECEDENCE: `date` is present but unreadable (0), so `timestamp` decides - first key that YIELDS A VALUE wins, not first key that is non-null
a null first key is skipped and the second key decides
an earlier key that places wins over a later key that would also place
a present-but-unreadable key outranks an absent one in the stated reason
a key list other than the comms one behaves the same way
RFC-3339 with an explicit +00:00 offset
RFC-3339 with Z
RFC-3339 with a sub-second fraction, truncated to the second
RFC-3339 with a non-UTC offset is placed at the instant, not the local clock
a date with no time of day is read as UTC midnight
the Unix epoch itself is an instant, not a falsy nothing
RFC-2822, the shape an email or MMS header arrives in
year 0100 is placed, far below the Unix epoch
year 2999 is placed - the reader has no ceiling, and adding one would reclassify four unrelated views' records as unusable
the empty string is a present value with no reading
a whitespace-only string is a present value with no reading
SQLite's magic word `now` must never mean the time of the query
a time of day with no date is not an instant
a bare numeric string is read as seconds, never as a Julian day
a signed integer literal is read in the same bands
surrounding whitespace does not stop a numeric string being read
a negative numeric string is not placed
exponent notation is read as the number it denotes
a hexadecimal literal is numeric but far below the band
the word Infinity is numeric to JavaScript and must still be refused
unparseable text is a present value with no reading
a JSON real in the seconds band is placed and its fraction truncated
a JSON real written in exponent form is placed
a JSON bool is a present value with no reading
a JSON object is a present value with no reading
a JSON array is a present value with no reading
JSON null is ABSENT, not a value that failed to read
every key absent is ABSENT
an empty metadata object is ABSENT
